The Volvo EX30 Cargo Version Qualifies for the UK's Zero Emission Van Grant
8 photos
Photo: Volvo
Not every business needs a conventional van to carry whatever they need transporting from point A to B. Some businesses also need a vehicle that is comfortable enough for long driving hours on a daily basis, as well as a vehicle whose footprint is small enough for the most urban of jungles.
Volvo has an answer to said requirements in the form of the EX30 Cargo, which is best described as a small crossover whose rear seats have been removed for additional cargo room. Converted for small commercial vehicle duties, the full-electric model now qualifies for the Zero Emission Van Grant in the United Kingdom.
Applying the £2,500 discount, you get a starting price of £33,529 on the road. Introduced in March 2026, the UK-market EX30 Cargo targets people who need a bit of usable load space without giving up the comfort of a passenger vehicle.
Beyond the rear bench's removal, the EX30 further boasts a black-painted bulkhead that separates the cabin from the cargo area. Modified rear side panels also need mentioning, and the doors have been modified to allow extended access to the cargo area. Of course, mounting points and cargo area illumination are standard as well.
The underfloor subframe customers don't see is key to said mounting points and the 390-kilogram payload, which can be alternatively read as 860 pounds. Volvo 's UK subsidiary further lists up to 1,000 liters (or 35.3 cubic feet). Based on these figures, you will realize that EX30 Cargo is not a replacement for compact vans.
This vehicle, instead, makes a lot of sense for small deliveries, service visits, and mobile workers whose daily kit fits in a smaller cargo area than you get from the likes of the Ford e-Transit Courier and Citroen e-Berlingo. Simply put, call it a niche commercial vehicle.
Photo: Volvo Over in the United Kingdom, the government recognizes the EX30 Cargo as a van despite not being one. The official list of eligible small electric vans also includes the Dacia Spring Cargo, which is derived from a passenger car as well. The small van grant provides up to 2,500 pounds sterling, and to qualify, a vehicle must meet three main requirements.
First and foremost, zero tailpipe CO2 emissions. The electric-only mandate continues with at least 60 miles (96 kilometers) of range without any emissions, and the final requirement is no more than 2,500 kilograms (5,512 pounds) in terms of gross vehicle weight.
A separate thing from the Electric Car Grant for passenger vehicles, the Zero Emission Van Grant is not unlimited. Per the government's web portal, only those who apply now can find out how many grants are currently available to distribute to eligible customers.
Prospective buyers are presented with two power levels, namely 150 hp for the P3 setup or 272 hp for those who upgrade to the P5. Advertised with best-in-class payload, the EX30 Cargo is good for 295 miles (475 kilometers) of range at most on a full charge in the WLTP.
Including variables like weather conditions, driving style, and payload, it goes without saying that its real-world range may be very different from what the Swedish automaker promises online.
